title: Palindrome Checker
story: You're texting a friend and type 'racecar'. You notice it reads the same backwards and forwards. Intrigued, you wonder: which other words have this magic property? Time to build a function that detects palindromes instantly.
why: Palindrome checking combines string length, while loops, and Boolean early returns — a compact real-world algorithm built from familiar pieces.
analogy: A palindrome check is like folding a piece of paper in half. When you fold 'racecar' down the middle, the 'r' touches 'r', the 'a' touches 'a', and the 'c' touches 'c'. If every pair matches at the fold, the word is a palindrome. A mismatch is like a torn edge — the fold doesn't line up.
try_it: Test is_palindrome with "madam", "kayak", "palindrome", and your own name. Then modify the function to ignore case by using string.str_lower() on the input before comparing.
tips: Start both pointers at opposite ends: left=0 and right=len-1
The loop condition `left < right` naturally handles odd and even length strings
Early return inside the loop is efficient — stop checking the moment you find a mismatch
Use string.str_len() to get the length before setting up pointers
common_mistakes: Setting right = len instead of len - 1 — strings are 0-indexed
Using <= instead of < in the loop condition — you'd compare the middle char with itself
Forgetting to update both left and right pointers inside the loop
Returning true inside the loop on a match — you must check ALL pairs first
